lacuna.name: checkpoint-resume-iterative-loops
lacuna.repo_anchor: The weco skill's local-mode reference states the loop's data layout: 'The configured agent harness (opencode) improves the code each step; the eval command measures it; the best result and every step land in `.weco/local-loop/`' and 'weco observe records locally under `.weco/observe/` (append-only JSONL)' (/home/dconnolly/.zcode/skills/weco/references/local-mode.md). An actual observe ledger on this host confirms the append-only shape: each line is {step, status, description, metrics, parent_step, logged_at} (/opt/repo/agentic-vllm/.weco/d256-bridge/.weco/observe/runs/a2341636.../steps.jsonl, 2026-09-06). The run brief records the gap this item researches: the local loop's steps.jsonl carries (value, improved_best, output tail per step) but 'keeps the BEST CODE only as the live working tree - no snapshots, no resume; an interrupted run restarts at step 0'. MEMORY.md (2026-09-08) shows the host already practices manual snapshot discipline for exactly this fragility outside weco: 'the vendored flash-attn campaign commits are archived as patches in the lane record (the tree is local-only, unwritable-origin, and lane-gitignored - the single point of failure is closed; rebuild = upstream v2.8.3 + git am in order)'. MEMORY.md (2026-09-07) plans multi-session weco ladders ('weco ladder on the M>=128 acceptance gap'), so the restart-at-step-0 loss window is real for planned work.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09, every domain that runs long iterative loops over mutable state has converged on the same three-part answer: (1) an append-only log as the source of truth, (2) an addressable snapshot of the mutated state, (3) a resume protocol that derives state from the log. Fuzzing: AFL++ (active, 4.x) resumes a campaign by re-running with '-i -' or AFL_AUTORESUME=1 against the existing output dir; the out dir IS the checkpoint (queue, fuzzer_stats, crashes, hangs) and everything needed to continue lives in that one directory; known caveats: resuming after manual queue trimming errors out, and the '>25 minutes of fuzzing' guard exists to stop accidental overwrites (aflplus.plus docs; discussions #2238, #1254). CI shops round-trip the out dir to S3 between jobs. LLM-agent scaffolds: Claude Code checkpointing captures file state BEFORE each user prompt (write-ahead ordering), keeps the 100 most recent per session, and /rewind restores code and/or conversation; bash-side file changes and symlinks are explicitly NOT covered, and it 'is not version control' (code.claude.com/docs). Shadow-git checkpointing is now an industry pattern: Cline commits workspace state into a separate shadow repo after each tool use so the main repo stays untouched; Gemini CLI, Tabnine, Kilo, Docker's agent, and Zoo Code document the same design; aider's earlier model auto-commits every edit to the user's own repo so /undo is a one-step revert (aider.chat/docs/git.html). OpenHands SDK (arXiv 2511.03690, 2025) persists base_state.json plus an append-only event directory with dual-path incremental writes (only new events flushed), resumes by loading base state and replaying events, and auto-detects incomplete/interrupted sessions. LangGraph (LangChain OSS docs, 2026) writes a checkpoint at each superstep boundary with pending-writes for completed sibling nodes, offers sync/async/exit durability modes ('async' and 'exit' can lose checkpoints on a process crash), and replay is at-least-once for external side effects (LLM calls and API requests are always re-triggered). SWE-agent writes a .traj JSON per run and 'sweagent run-replay' re-executes saved actions. Evolutionary LLM optimizers: OpenEvolve (PyPI 0.2.2, Apache-2.0, open AlphaEvolve implementation) saves checkpoint_N/ dirs every checkpoint_interval (default 10 iterations) containing best_program.py, best_program_info.json, programs/ (the whole program database) and metadata.json; '--checkpoint dir' resumes, loading all evolved programs and continuing numbering. AutoML: Optuna (JournalStorage stabilized in 4.0, Nov 2024) is the cleanest append-only analog: an operation journal on file/NFS, state rebuilt by replay into an in-memory snapshot with incremental sync by log number and an optional pickle snapshot to skip replay; its JournalFileBackend.read_logs (verified in source, optuna/storages/journal/_file.py) tolerates an in-flight partial tail line via a remaining-log-size bound taken at open time but raises on a permanently corrupt line; RDB studies resume via create_study(load_if_exists=True); a heartbeat mechanism reaps trials whose process died (stale RUNNING -> FAIL) and RetryFailedTrialCallback re-runs them. Ray Tune Tuner.restore requires the full experiment directory including trial checkpoints and resumes uncompleted trials. Notebook executors: jupyter-cache keys executed notebooks by content hash so unchanged notebooks are skipped (used by Jupyter Book/MyST-NB/Quarto) - deterministic re-execution as cache. DVC 2.0 (Feb 2021) shipped checkpoint experiments (an ephemeral git commit per checkpoint stage, 'dvc exp run' resumes, '--reset' restarts) but announced their deprecation for the next major version, wound down in the 3.x line [uncertain: exact removal version]. Build systems: Bazel has no resume flag; the action cache and output tree survive restarts so a re-run after a crash re-validates completed actions instead of re-executing them, and a corrupted action cache index causes a cache reset and full rebuild (bazel issue #3043), with remote/disk cache as the mitigation. Sandboxes/CoW: Firecracker documents full and diff microVM snapshots (CPU+memory+devices) and is 'optimized for fast load/resume'; practice reports restore in ~4-28 ms and ~100 ms CoW 'fork' of a snapshotted agent sandbox via MAP_PRIVATE [uncertain: timings are blog-reported, not from the official doc]. Theory: WAL/ARIES (database literature) states the ordering rule that closes the phantom window - the log record must reach stable storage BEFORE the mutation is treated as committed, and redo must be idempotent so replaying a partially-applied history is safe; 'repeat history' recovery replays the log rather than guessing intent.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers to the weco-local long-range runner: (1) The log is already right. steps.jsonl as append-only JSONL matches Optuna's journal and OpenHands' event stream; what is missing is that 'improved_best' points at the LIVE TREE instead of at an addressable artifact. Every surveyed system makes the incumbent durable and addressable: AFL's queue, OpenEvolve's best_program.py inside checkpoint dirs, Cline/aider git commits, Optuna trial records with parameters+values. Concretely: the loop should snapshot the tree per step (or per improved_best) in the lane-local git the host already uses (same discipline as the flash-attn patch archive in MEMORY.md) and write the commit sha into the step record; a shadow repo keeps main history clean if the lane is the primary repo. (2) Ordering closes the phantom window. The brief's failure case - crash between tree mutation and log append - is the textbook WAL inversion; the fix used by Claude Code (snapshot before the mutation) or by OpenEvolve (record points at an already-written artifact) makes the log the ONLY claim of truth: on resume, discard any tree state not referenced by a log line (git reset --hard to the best sha) and continue at step N+1. A step whose eval finished but whose log line never landed is wasted work, never a phantom best. (3) Resume = re-run the same command against the same directory (AFL_AUTORESUME semantics); keep everything needed to continue inside .weco/local-loop/ (log + git refs + config), which this host's single-writer, single-machine loop can do without Optuna's NFS locking machinery. (4) Tail-tolerant reads: append each record with a single write() and have the loader skip an unterminated last line (Optuna's remaining-log-size trick), so a crash mid-append costs one record, not the file. (5) Mark in-flight steps in the log itself (status: started/completed/failed plus parent sha), Optuna RUNNING-trial style, so a watchdog can fail a hung step and resume re-derives from the last completed parent. (6) Keep-best-on-eval is cheap: a git commit per step costs milliseconds; OpenEvolve's every-10 default exists because it snapshots a whole program database, weco snapshots a diff. Does NOT transfer: LangGraph-style checkpointed agent-state graphs (the artifact of record here is the tree, not a channel state); jupyter-cache-style content-hash skipping of re-evaluation (this host's own cross-restart variance doctrine - median-of-N, MEMORY.md 2026-09-07 - means resumed steps must re-eval, never trust a cached metric value); Bazel-style action-cache resume (weco steps are not pure functions of inputs - the tree mutates and the model is nondeterministic - so 're-run is cheap' does not hold; snapshot instead); DVC checkpoint experiments as a tool (deprecated upstream; adopt the ephemeral-commit idea, not the tool); Firecracker/CoW microVM snapshots (only worth it if eval-environment cold start dominates; this host's systemd/chroot sandbox already restores fast enough for kernel evals).

design.mechanism: Per-step five-phase protocol in the local-loop runner, all inside .weco/local-loop/: (Phase 1) append an intent record {step: N, status: 'started', parent: <sha of step N-1 snapshot>} and flush. (Phase 2) let the harness mutate the working tree. (Phase 3) snapshot: `git add -A; git commit` in the lane repo (a dedicated lane-local or shadow repo whose history never leaves the lane) -> sha_N; the untracked/uncommitted residue case is captured by -A, so the snapshot is total. (Phase 4) run the eval under the existing timeout/watchdog. (Phase 5) append the completion record {step: N, sha: sha_N, value, improved_best, output_tail} as ONE write() to steps.jsonl, fsync, and if improved_best then update the ref `weco/best` (a git tag or branch) to sha_N. Resume procedure (idempotent, re-runnable): (a) load steps.jsonl, skipping an unterformed/undecodable last line; (b) take the last record with status 'completed'; if none, start at step 0; (c) `git reset --hard weco/best` (the incumbent) - any tree state not referenced by a completed log line is by construction discarded; (d) continue the loop at N+1 with the optimizer told the incumbent context from the log (OpenHands replay semantics). Atomicity contract: the CLAIM (log line) is only written after the ARTIFACT (commit) exists - WAL order - so a crash can waste a step but never fabricate one; the eval itself is never trusted across restarts (values are re-derivable, incumbents are not). Optionally rotate a full snapshot of steps.jsonl (Optuna's pickle-snapshot analog) if the log grows large. The gate against silent skips: at run close, assert worktree HEAD == weco/best sha and steps.jsonl is newline-terminated.
design.failure_modes: Known failure modes and defenses from the surveyed systems: (1) Phantom step (crash between tree mutation and log append) - closed by the commit-before-append order above; without it the run believes an unlogged tree is step N (the exact weco-local restart-at-0 hazard generalized). (2) Torn tail (crash mid-append corrupts the last JSONL line) - tail-tolerant loader; Optuna raises on a corrupt NON-tail line, so also keep a periodic full-log snapshot or accept hard failure with a clear error. (3) Hung eval between snapshot and append - the 'started' intent record plus the existing watchdog marks the step failed; resume re-derives from parent (Optuna heartbeat/fail_stale_trials pattern; its absence leaves orphaned RUNNING trials forever, optuna issues #913/#3384). (4) Silent skip / drift between tree and log - post-run assertion HEAD==weco/best; git status non-empty after a completed step means someone mutated outside the loop (Claude Code has the same hole: bash-side changes are untracked). (5) Poisoned metrics on resume - NEVER reuse a logged value as if re-measured; this host's cross-restart variance doctrine makes cached values worse than useless; resume re-evaluates (the anti-jupyter-cache). (6) History pollution / repo bloat - use a lane-local or shadow repo (Cline/aider lesson: aider pollutes the user's real history; shadow repos were invented to stop that); gc periodically. (7) Concurrent writers on shared storage - Optuna JournalStorage's distributed failures (#6084) came from NFS assumptions; the local loop stays single-writer by construction. (8) Checkpoint-cache corruption after a hard crash (Bazel #3043 analog) - the git object store is the cache; `git fsck` on resume, and worst case rebuild from the patch archive like the flash-attn lane already does. (9) Best-by-luck vs best-by-value: improved_best must be recomputed from the log at resume (max/min over completed records), not trusted from a torn ref update.
design.effort_estimate: Wrapper/fork-level, small: the local-loop runner already owns mutate+eval+append, so adding the git commit phase, the started/completed statuses, the weco/best ref, and the tail-tolerant loader/resume branch is on the order of a few hundred lines in the weco local fork (no upstream weco or cloud changes; git is already the lane's substrate). Doctrine-only addition: a resume runbook step ('re-run the same command against the same .weco/local-loop dir').
design.priority_signal: For: this is the single mechanism that converts a multi-day weco ladder from 'one crash away from step 0' to an interruptible campaign; the host's GPU-lease windows and cross-restart median-of-N discipline make each step expensive (minutes-to-hours of eval), so losing the incumbent tree loses the whole campaign's compounding; the host has already been burned once (flash-attn lane archived as patches precisely because the tree was the single point of failure); the implementation is cheap (git commits) and the pattern is validated independently by AFL++, Optuna, OpenHands, OpenEvolve, Claude Code/Cline, and 40 years of WAL. Against: single-writer single-machine means no distributed complexity to solve, and if campaigns stay shorter than the eval-timeout granularity the window rarely bites; git snapshots on huge worktrees (the vLLM lane) could add per-step cost (mitigated: commit only the tuned kernel files or use a lane-scoped shadow repo). Net: load-bearing for multi-day unattended campaigns on this host; implement before the next multi-window weco ladder, not after the first crash.
